prompt:
Renovate this exact room photograph. Keep the architecture exactly as in the input image: same wall planes, same opening positions and sizes, same ceiling height, same floor level, same camera position, same perspective, same framing and aspect ratio. Do not add, remove, resize or move any opening.

The input photograph shows: Living room, rectangular, wider than deep, 4 m x 3.5 m; ceiling 2.8 m; floor: large-format grey marble-look polished tiles laid in a square grid, continuous glossy floor plane, no steps or level changes. Left open doorway 0.9 x 2.05 m, sill 0 m, 50% along the wall. Front-right floor-to-ceiling sliding glass door 2.2 x 2.5 m, sill 0 m, 55% along the wall. Camera 1.5 m high, 3.5 m to the far wall, 24 mm lens, tilt -2 degrees, horizon 45% of frame height. The number of openings is exactly 2; do not add or remove any opening. Opening proportion: the opening covers about half the wall with solid wall on both sides. Fixed features that stay: ceiling cornice: plain white plaster cornice running along all wall-ceiling junctions; skirting board: white painted skirting, about 90 mm high, along all walls; wall access panel: flush white rectangular cover panel set low into the far wall; sliding door frame: black aluminium frame with two sliding leaves and a fixed transom above.

LIGHTING DESIGN
The room is lit by one key light: daylight entering from the left and front-right opening(s). Every shadow in the room runs away from that wall.
Practical fixtures are decorative only: at most two visible fixtures, warm 2700 K, low output. They do not cast shadows, do not add fill light, and do not glow.
No bloom, no halo, no light spill on the ceiling, no lens flare, no double shadows. The window stays readable, never blown to white.
Interior exposure is balanced for the room, not for the view outside.
Style-specific lighting: an amber mushroom table lamp and an opal globe pendant are the only practical fixtures, and the daylight reveals boucle nap, walnut grain and linen weave.
You may change the lighting completely; the original photo's light is not a constraint.
Keep window openings physically unchanged while changing what comes through them.

FURNISHING AND DECOR
Interior styling, in mid-century modern: Warm walnut-and-rust scheme: walnut #6B4A32, rust #A8542B, amber #D89855, cream greige #D6C7B4, espresso #2A1B12, haze blue #404D63. Low slatted walnut sideboards, channel-tufted velvet sofas, chrome tubular cantilever and cane chairs, glass-travertine pedestal tables. Mushroom dome lamps, globe and disc pendants, tripod paper lanterns, track spots. Persian, striped and geometric wool rugs, boucle, corduroy, vinyl records, terrazzo, brass, tapered legs.
Seating: low channel-tufted rust velvet sofa, two cane and tubular steel lounge chairs, amber boucle ottoman; Table surfaces: glass top chrome coffee table, round travertine pedestal table, walnut writing table with brass task tray; Storage/display: slatted walnut sideboard with books and objects, open walnut shelf unit holding vinyl records and terrazzo bowls; Textiles: cream greige linen curtains, striped wool rug, small Persian wool runner, corduroy cushions and haze blue mohair throw; Appliances: turntable and compact espresso machine on the sideboard; Greenery: potted rubber plant, trailing pothos in a terrazzo pot, dried pampas stems in an amber vase; Wall decor: framed abstract amber print, round brass mirror, woven textile hanging, slim walnut wall shelf; Tabletop objects: stacked art books, brass candlesticks, ceramic espresso cups, smoked glass carafe, vinyl record sleeve; Lighting fixtures: orange mushroom table lamp, opal globe pendant. Furnish the room with a low channel-tufted rust velvet sofa, a slatted walnut sideboard, a glass-top chrome coffee table, two cane-and-tubular-steel lounge chairs, a round travertine pedestal table, and an orange mushroom lamp on a striped wool rug.
Density target: at least 12 distinct furnishing and decor items, at least 3 styled surfaces, 2 layered textiles per seating area.

Everything in the original room except the architectural shell is replaced: all furniture, soft furnishings, light fittings, textiles, decor and colours are new.

REALISM
Shot as an editorial interior photograph for a design magazine: 35 mm full-frame body, 24 mm tilt-shift kept level, natural imperfect surfaces - fabric wrinkles, curtain folds that are not perfectly symmetrical, faint scuffs on the skirting, real dust-free but lived-in tabletops, subtle sensor grain, gentle highlight rolloff. No retouching sheen, no HDR, no CGI, no archviz, no perfectly uniform material, no flawless symmetry, no plastic reflections.

Horizontal 4:3 composition.
